# HMPFL Week 2 Recap: Cell Block Chaos

The bars rattled and the warden's whistle blew all weekend long as HMPFL Week 2 delivered drama, a shootout for the ages, and at least one inmate who should probably be placed on suicide watch after this beatdown.

## The Nail-Biter: Rice, Rice Baby Escapes by a Hair

In the tightest cell check of the week, **Rice, Rice Baby ✨** narrowly avoided lockdown, edging **Hernandez Hitmen** 191.1 to 190.35 — a margin of just 0.75 points. That's the fantasy equivalent of sneaking a shiv past the metal detector. Davante Adams (67.0) and CeeDee Lamb (58.6) both balled out for Hernandez, but it wasn't enough to spring them from this one. Somewhere, a guard is writing up a disciplinary report for "insufficient bench depth."

## The Blowout: Massage Boys Give OJ's Bronco the Full Treatment

**The Massage Boys** put **OJ's Denver Bronco** in a chokehold, winning 194.0 to 163.4 — a 30.6-point margin that's the largest of the week. Jaxon Smith-Njigba exploded for a ridiculous 73.5 points, essentially doing all the heavy lifting himself while OJ's roster sat there like it was waiting for a parole hearing that's never coming.

## Honorable Mention Beatdown: The Shootout Nobody Saw Coming

While the numbers say Massage Boys' win was the biggest gap, the real war crime happened between **Ruggs, Drugs and TDs** and **Glove Don't Fit, Blitz**, who combined for a jaw-dropping 525.9 points. Glove Don't Fit prevailed 278.2–247.7, propelled by Amon-Ra St. Brown's 56.9-point outing, even as Ruggs, Drugs and TDs got a two-QB showcase from Dak Prescott (60.1) and Jared Goff (59.1) that would win most weeks — just not this one.

## The Big House MVP: Josh Allen Breaks Out of Solitary

No performance this week deserves a full pardon more than **Josh Allen**, who dropped a preposterous 78.6 points for Josh Allen's Prison Cell. Unfortunately, even a QB1 overall performance for the ages wasn't enough — his squad still fell 207.75–226.55 to Steve Ruggs, who got just enough from Brock Purdy (59.7) to survive. Allen's stat line should honestly come with a "time served" reduction.
